sections.title: Player text
sections.body: The Custodian gathers what she needs with the brisk energy of someone much younger than she looks. "The Open Vale is where the ward was first forged," she says. "It is where it must be renewed." She looks at each of you in turn. "I cannot do this alone, and what comes for us when the magic rises will not be gentle. But I think you already knew the job was bigger than a crate." When you are ready, the treehouse unfolds one last time, and the road to the Open Vale opens before you.

Gmprivate: Convergence math: high trust + deep understanding + ready prep = ward_stability stable. Otherwise fragile. If package_status=lost, commitment can exist emotionally but Act 5 cannot proceed normally until the recovery branch is confirmed.
Playertakeaway: You are choosing the hard road on purpose, and what you do before you walk it will keep you alive.
Storytakeaway: The party chooses to finish what the job started, not just because of pay but because the stakes are now real.
Mechanictakeaway: Preparation is the mechanic: rest, learn, spend boons, and plan; ritual_prep and ward_stability set the Act 5 countdown pressure.

Storyscope: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end. Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy. The sealed package is the capital's ward Keystone; the city is unwarded while it is away. KEEP GUARANTEED "The wood never needed managing. It needed leaving alone." ADD SEED "Your capital's safety is older than your contracts. It is the very thing they teach you to fear." ADD SEED The Keystone's magic is pre-corporate forest-ward work, the same school companies call primitive. ADD EARNED Knowledge Hard 20 The Custodian glances at obsolete Soulspire inspection seals on her counterweight boulder. ADD EARNED Instinct Medium 15 Presence: earn candor. Knowledge: place the magic. Instinct: read the Custodian's fear.
